title: Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization
data_curation: Preference data comes from Reddit TL;DR summarization and AnthropicHH dialogue. Reddit TL;DR provides SFT data (117k/6k/6k train/val/test) and human feedback data Dhf (93k preferences over decodes from multiple models); AnthropicHH helpful slice has 161k/9k train/test, with positive responses used as SFT targets. Cross-task transfer is probed on CNN/DailyMail (287k/13k/11k, fine-tune data only). Core data construction is generative: sample 64 response candidates from the SFT policy (temperature 0.7, top-k=40), sub-sample 8 via statistical rejection sampling, then label pairs with a T5-XXL (11B) pairwise reward-ranking model trained on Dhf. Reward-model validation accuracy is 73.23% (summarization) and 69.75% (AI assistant); the gold PaLM 2-S reward model reaches 76.07%/70.18%. Three preference-pair variants are compared: direct (use Dhf), sft-sample-rank, and rso-sample-rank.
curriculum: A single-round, staged offline pipeline: (1) train an SFT policy on Dsft; (2) train a pairwise T5-XXL reward-ranking model on Dhf; (3) sample candidates from the SFT policy and apply statistical rejection sampling guided by the reward to approximate samples from the optimal policy, then label pairs with the reward model; (4) fit the policy with a classification loss on these labeled pairs. Checkpoints are selected by highest reward-model win rate against the SFT target. Sampling/ranking prompts are drawn from the SFT training set. Rationale: since the MLE of the optimal policy wants pairs sampled from π*, drawing from the reward-induced optimal policy πrψ is closer to on-policy online RLHF than directly fitting on Dhf (DPO) or sampling only from the SFT policy (SLiC). One round mirrors one round of ReST; the authors note RSO can be iterated over multiple rounds.
method: RSO (Statistical Rejection Sampling Optimization) is the contribution. The motivating observation: DPO's MLE requires preference pairs drawn from the optimal policy π*, yet DPO uses pairs from mixed unknown policies and SLiC can only sample from the SFT policy. RSO uses Neal (2003) statistical rejection sampling with the SFT policy as proposal and a pointwise reward rψ derived from the pairwise T5-XXL reward model: accept an SFT sample y with probability exp((rψ(y)-rmax)/β), giving samples from πrψ. β trades reward exploitation against SFT regularization; β→0 reduces to top-k-over-N/best-of-N (a shown special case, prone to reward hacking), β→∞ keeps the SFT policy. The paper also unifies losses: DPO is logistic regression on preferences (sigmoid-norm) and SLiC is essentially an SVM with hinge loss; it introduces hinge-norm (SVM counterpart of DPO) and decouples the loss temperature γ from β. Theorem 1 gives the expected acceptance rate of the sampling-without-replacement algorithm.
eval_metrics: Four evaluators: Proxy Reward Model (win rate vs SFT target on the trained T5-XXL reward model), Gold Reward Model (PaLM 2-S trained on the same data), AutoSxS (PaLM 2-L few-shot pairwise win rate, tie-aware), and Human Evaluation (Amazon Mechanical Turk side-by-side with pointwise 1-5 quality and a best-choice vote, 3 raters per task). On T5-large, RSO sigmoid-norm rso-sample-rank reaches 92.37% Proxy / 84.40% Gold / 71.86% AutoSxS on Reddit TL;DR vs DPO's 84.35 / 76.09 / 58.65; on AnthropicHH 86.94 / 69.26 / 40.98 vs 51.63 / 67.72 / 24.01. Scaling to T5-XXL, RSO improves AutoSxS over DPO by +1.1% (TL;DR) and +33.1% (AnthropicHH). Human eval selects RSO >2x as often as DPO on both tasks. Ablations find β=0.5, γ=0.05 optimal and first-round-rank best for rso-8-sample.
key_results: RSO (T5-large, sigmoid-norm, rso-sample-rank) reaches 84.40% Gold Reward and 71.86% AutoSxS on Reddit TL;DR vs DPO 76.09/58.65, and 69.26/40.98 on AnthropicHH vs 67.72/24.01. At T5-XXL scale, RSO improves AutoSxS over DPO by +1.1% (TL;DR) and +33.1% (AnthropicHH); human raters choose RSO >2x more often than DPO.
evolution_note: RSO reacts to DPO and SLiC (both 2023), arguing that DPO's MLE is mismatched because preference pairs are not sampled from the optimal policy, and that best-of-N rejection sampling (AnthropicHH, Llama2) is an unregularized special case. By using reward-guided statistical rejection sampling to approximate on-policy data, it bridges offline preference optimization and online RLHF, foreshadowing later iterative-DPO and best-of-N / on-policy preference methods that emphasize sampling from the learned policy.
